---
title: "Top-p Sampling"
description: "A decoding method that samples from the smallest set of top-ranked tokens whose cumulative probability reaches p."
term: "Top-p Sampling"
letter: "T"
category: "LLM Engineering"
difficulty: "Intermediate"
---

## Simple explanation

Top-p sampling, also called nucleus sampling, keeps the smallest set of
likely next tokens whose probabilities add up to at least a chosen
threshold $p$. It adapts the number of choices to how concentrated the
model's predictions are.

## Technical explanation

After sorting token probabilities in descending order, top-p decoding
retains the shortest prefix whose cumulative probability reaches or
exceeds $p$, then samples from the renormalized set. Implementations may
combine top-p with temperature or top-k filtering.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

An adaptive candidate set can preserve variety when the model is uncertain
while excluding low-probability tails when its distribution is peaked.
Values of $p$ and interactions with other decoding controls affect output
diversity and reliability.

## How it works

The decoder computes next-token probabilities, sorts candidates, and
accumulates probability mass until reaching the selected threshold. It
masks tokens outside that nucleus, renormalizes the retained probabilities,
and samples the next token.

## Practical example

To compare top-p settings for a response-generation system, generate
multiple outputs for a fixed prompt set and measure validity, diversity,
and task success. Keep temperature and all other settings unchanged during
the comparison.

## Common misconceptions

- The parameter $p$ is not the fixed number of tokens retained; that
  number varies at each step.
- Top-p sampling does not guarantee factual or coherent output.
